card.name: Litefeet
card.tagline: Harlem's 2006 street dance where dancers perform with weightless 'light feet'.
card.profile: Litefeet, also referred to as 'getting lite,' is a street dance and vernacular dance that emerged from Harlem, New York, in the early 2000s and was established in 2006. The dance incorporates elements like the Harlem shake, shuffling, and shoe tricks, and is famously performed on New York City subways during 'Showtime' performances. Driven by fast-paced 100-110 BPM rap beats and drum kits, Litefeet has become an enduring symbol of Harlem's urban musical social scene.
card.insight: In 2006 Harlem, dancers developed Litefeet to feel weightless, performing fast-paced routines known as 'Showtime' on New York subways.
sources: Source: Litefeet on Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0. Read: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Litefeet
card.profile_long: Litefeet, also referred to as 'getting lite,' is a type of street dance and vernacular dance that emerged from Harlem, New York in the early 2000s and was established in 2006. The term comes from dancers dancing as though they have 'light feet,' or are weightless. The Harlem shake is commonly incorporated into the social dance Litefeet, as is the Chicken Noodle Soup, the Tone Wop, the Rev Up, and the Aunt Jackie. Other popular Litefeet dances include the Bad One and the All In. Moves often include shuffling, hat tricks, and shoe tricks. Dancers often perform on subways in New York City, where the performances are called Showtime, and at Union Square. The dance has been embraced as a symbol of the urban musical social scene of Harlem. Well-known teams include W.A.F.F.L.E. (We Are Family For Life, Ent.), MonzterInc, Brotherhood, 2Real Boyz, Team Rocket, Demon, 2crafty, Loonatics, Outsiders, Live Zombies, LyveTyme, NewMem The Litefeet Collective, and Bwreckfast Club E.A.T. Litefeet is also the name of the music played along with the dance, often fast-paced 100-110BPM rap beats and drum kits. LiL LIVE, HANN, M-Lyve, Kid the Wiz, Dsparkz, Fliqht, TweekTune, BSNYEA, H Rockz, Faro, AG the Voice of Harlem, SGFLOW, Lil Sns, Aye Jae Beats, Coma, Lady MoSoFou, DJ Webstar, and Young B are some well-known Litefeet music producers.

observation.dancers: Mixed group of men, women, and a child; solo dancers taking turns performing in the center while others watch, cheer, and clap in a circle.
observation.formation_and_space: Circular formation with dancers gathered around an open central space where individuals take turns performing solos.
observation.posture: Upright and athletic torso, knees slightly bent with weight shifting quickly, dynamic and energetic posture.
observation.footwork: Rapid stepping, high knee raises, shuffling, quick hops, and bounces on the beat; exact heel/toe contact cannot be fully discerned due to video compression and rapid motion.
observation.arms_and_hands: Arms pump, swing, and reach dynamically with the rhythm; hands are sometimes loose, clenched, or gesturing; no objects held.
observation.hips_and_torso: Torso bounces and twists with the energetic footwork; hips move naturally with the quick steps and drops.
observation.levels_jumps_turns: Frequent jumps, drops to the floor/squats, and sudden level changes with occasional turns.
observation.costume_and_props: Casual streetwear including t-shirts, hoodies, track jackets, jeans, leggings, and sneakers; backpacks and water bottles on the sidewalk.
observation.cannot_infer: Exact foot placement, subtle weight shifts, and precise ankle articulation are obscured by rapid camera motion and video compression.
